research_goal: Design and implement a Python deep-research-agent readiness checker for long-form source-grounded report generation.
coding_context: agent-platform uses Python dataclasses and deterministic CLI commands for planning and evaluation agents.
source_value_provenance: Deep research report stages <- OpenAI, Exa, LangChain docs checked 2026-06-01
Citation verification risk <- Cited but Not Verified and ReportBench papers checked 2026-06-01
Python dataclass/argparse pattern <- Python official docs plus existing agent-platform CLI code
plan_evidence: Separate module <- existing research_insight_planner.py is planning readiness, not report readiness
CLI name complete-deep-research <- existing complete-coding-research naming pattern
Tests should mirror test_research_insight_planner.py and test_coding_research.py deterministic gap checks
stack_version_constraints: Use repository's current Python 3 execution path; avoid new dependencies.
Keep code compatible with existing Python unittest and dataclass style.
issue_discussion_notes: Open-source deep research examples commonly split research into parallel or focused lanes and synthesize a final cited report.
Community discussions mention workflow-based implementations to avoid pure-agent loops and token waste.
community_signal_notes: GitHub stars and Reddit comments were used as discovery and adoption signals, not proof of correctness.
The implementation relies on official docs and papers for factual claims, while community sources inform risks and usage patterns.
language_options: TypeScript/Node in workspace-monitor or a separate tool
language_decision_notes: Python matches existing planning/evaluation agents and CLI structure.
TypeScript would split shared agent logic across runtimes without clear benefit for this readiness checker.
code_reference_notes: Use frozen dataclass input plus from_dict conversion and deterministic gap list pattern.
Expose one CLI command that loads JSON and prints a stable JSON report.
Tests should assert status and exact gap messages for missing critical fields.
Open-source references show deep research often needs planning, parallel/focused sub-research, and final synthesis.
architecture_practitioner_sources: Reddit Open Source Deep Research discussions
architecture_options: Extend research_insight_planner.py with deep report fields
architecture_decision_notes: Selected separate deep_research.py because deep report readiness has different fields and thresholds from plan readiness.
Keeping modules separate avoids weakening the simpler research-insight planner with long-report-specific constraints.
architecture_tradeoff_notes: A separate checker adds one more CLI command but keeps responsibilities clear.
Future real search automation can call this checker after retrieval and synthesis.
folder_structure_options: Add code under agent-platform/src/agent_platform/planning with tests under agent-platform/tests
folder_structure_decision_notes: Selected agent-platform because this is a shared agent capability and mirrors coding-research-agent.
_tools would be better for deterministic crawling or report conversion tools, not agent readiness policy.
folder_semantics_notes: _ops/workflows and _ops/prompts expose the reusable operating path.
maintainability_notes: Use the existing tuple-of-strings validation helpers style.
Keep thresholds as constants so tests document the policy.
Avoid adding runtime dependencies in this first version.
findings: Deep research report generation needs planning, iterative retrieval, extraction, synthesis, citations, and skeptical review.
Citation presence is insufficient unless checked against source support.
Existing agent-platform patterns are enough for a deterministic readiness checker.
options: Install an external deep research framework now
recommendation: Add a separate no-dependency Python readiness checker and defer external search framework installation until a concrete retrieval integration is required.

post_research_answers.what_was_verified: Verified deep research stage patterns, citation audit risks, existing Python agent-platform implementation style, and open-source reference patterns.
post_research_answers.best_option: Separate Python deep_research.py readiness checker plus config/template/docs.
post_research_answers.why_this_option: It fits existing agent-platform boundaries, avoids new dependencies, and keeps report-readiness separate from plan-readiness.
post_research_answers.alternatives_rejected: Extending research_insight_planner.py would blur responsibilities. Installing LangChain Deep Agents now is premature because the user asked for the platform agent structure, not a live retrieval backend.
post_research_answers.implementation_impact: Add planning module, CLI command, tests, configs, docs, workflow, prompt, memory/bootstrap references, and history artifacts.
post_research_answers.risks_and_unknowns: No real crawler is installed in this first version. Citation audit still depends on checking source content.
post_research_answers.validation_plan: Run unit tests, complete-deep-research sample, config contract, memory bootstrap, workspace health, grounding, and work evaluator.
post_research_answers.reusable_knowledge: Capture deep research stage model and citation audit requirements in config, docs, workflow, and prompt.

validation_steps: Run config contract and memory bootstrap checks.
risks_or_unknowns: The first version validates completed research packages, not retrieval execution.
Thresholds may need tuning after several real deep research reports.
